proposal.title: Synthesis of Foundational Assumption Testing in Intelligent Systems
proposal.summary: This research synthesizes evidence concerning the capability of intelligent systems to identify and correct internal reasoning limitations. Foundational assumptions—such as the inherent consistency of a formal system or the alignment between reasoning and final output—often mask underlying operational limits. Evidence from Gödel’s Incompleteness Theorems (source-e42e8586cd12475d) demonstrates that consistent formal systems cannot prove their own consistency, establishing a hard limit on self-contained verification. Conversely, contemporary AI research into 'reasoning-answer hit gaps' (source-d595268483b94a8e) shows that models may possess correct information during reasoning segments but fail to incorporate it into final outputs. This reveals a gap between reasoning performance and output fidelity, identifying a flawed assumption that reasoning flow automatically yields correct results.
